# Controls
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/behavior/controls

Set boundaries and controls for your agent's capabilities

Set boundaries to keep your agent focused, accurate, and aligned with your business goals.

## Key Controls

* **Stay On Topic**: Keep conversations focused on your main business purpose and avoid derailing
* **Hallucination Prevention**: Ground responses in facts and information you've provided
* **Define Capabilities**: Clearly specify what your agent can and cannot do for visitors
* **Content Boundaries**: Set limits on topics, actions, and information sharing


# First Message
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/behavior/first-message

Configure the initial greeting your agent sends to visitors

Set up the opening message your agent will use when starting conversations with visitors.

## Message Configuration

Create a welcoming and informative first message that:

* **Introduces the agent**: Let customers know they're talking to an AI assistant
* **Sets expectations**: Explain what kind of help is available
* **Offers guidance**: Suggest common questions or topics
* **Maintains brand voice**: Align with your company's communication style


# Human Fallback
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/behavior/human-fallback

Configure when your agent escalates to human assistance

Your agent can automatically mark conversations as requiring human assistance when certain situations arise.

## When Agent Escalates

* **Complex Inquiries**: Questions beyond the agent's knowledge
* **User Requests**: When someone specifically asks to speak with a human
* **Sentiment Detection**: Frustrated or upset visitors
* **Custom Scenarios**: Specific situations you define that require human assistance


# Instructions
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/behavior/instructions

Define what your agent does and the journey it creates for visitors

Define your agent's core purpose and the experience you want to create for every visitor. Instructions tell your agent what it's trying to accomplish and how to guide visitors through your desired flow.

## What to Define

**Agent Purpose**: What does your agent do? Is it qualifying leads, providing product information, scheduling demos, or handling support inquiries?

**Primary Goal**: What's the main outcome you want from each conversation? A qualified lead, a scheduled call, a purchase, or a resolved question?

**Visitor Journey**: What flow should visitors experience? How do you want to guide them from initial interest to your desired action?

**Success Criteria**: How do you know when your agent has successfully completed its job with a visitor?


# Personality
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/behavior/personality

Define your agent's personality traits and communication style

Shape your agent's personality to align with your brand and create engaging customer interactions.

## Personality Traits

Configure traits that influence how your agent communicates:

* **Friendliness Level**: From professional to casual
* **Enthusiasm**: How energetic and positive responses should be
* **Empathy**: Sensitivity to customer emotions and concerns
* **Confidence**: Assertiveness in providing information and solutions


# Tone
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/behavior/tone

Set the communication tone for your agent's interactions

Configure how your agent communicates with prospects and customers through tone and style preferences.

## Tone Options

* **Professional**: Formal business communication
* **Friendly**: Warm and approachable interactions
* **Casual**: Relaxed and conversational style
* **Empathetic**: Understanding and supportive responses
* **Direct**: Clear and to-the-point communication
* **Custom**: Define your own unique tone that matches your brand voice

## Tone Consistency

Ensure your agent maintains consistent tone across all interactions while adapting appropriately to different prospect and customer needs.


# Verbosity
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/behavior/verbosity

Control the length and detail level of your agent's responses

Control how much detail your agent provides in responses - from brief and direct to comprehensive and explanatory.


# Articles
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/content/articles

Create and manage custom articles for your agent's knowledge base

Add custom text content directly to your agent's knowledge base. Articles are simply text-based information that your agent can reference when responding to prospects and customers.

Create articles with any information you want your agent to know - product details, company policies, FAQs, or any other relevant content your agent should be able to discuss.


# Files
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/content/files

Upload and manage files for your agent's knowledge base

Upload documents, PDFs, spreadsheets, and other files to enhance your agent's knowledge and capabilities.

## Supported File Types

* **Documents**: PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT
* **Spreadsheets**: XLS, XLSX, CSV
* **Presentations**: PPT, PPTX
* **Images**: PNG, JPG, JPEG, GIF

## File Management

Upload files that your agent can reference when responding to customer inquiries. Files are automatically processed and indexed for quick retrieval.


# Websites
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/content/websites

Connect websites and web pages to your agent's knowledge base

Allow your agent to access and reference information from specific websites and web pages.

## Website Integration

Add websites that your agent can crawl and reference for up-to-date information.


# Design
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/design

Customize the visual appearance and interaction features of your agent interface

Agents can be configured to best align with your business branding and colors for a seamless brand experience. The Design tab also includes powerful interaction features that enhance how visitors engage with your agent.

## Key Design Features

* **Brand Alignment**: Customize colors, fonts, and visual elements to match your business branding
* **White-label Option**: Use Dimedove agents without "Powered by Dimedove" notices for complete brand consistency
* **Smart Replies**: Toggle AI-powered reply suggestions that adapt to conversation flow to optimize engagement

## Interaction Features

### Attachments

<Info>Attachments are available to teams on the Pro subscription.</Info>

Enable file and image sharing to give visitors the ability to share documents and images directly in their conversations with your agent. When enabled, visitors can upload files using the attachment button in the chat interface.

**Supported Files**:

* Most popular image formats for sharing screenshots, photos, and visual content
* Common document formats including PDFs, spreadsheets, presentations, and text files

**Benefits**:

* **Richer Context**: Visitors can share supporting documents, invoices, contracts, or images that provide context to their questions
* **Document Analysis**: Your agent can analyze and extract information from shared files, reducing the need for visitors to manually describe document contents
* **Reduced Back-and-Forth**: Instead of lengthy explanations, visitors can simply share the relevant file and let the agent extract the necessary information
* **Higher Quality Data**: Collect files directly from conversations for more complete records and follow-up

### Dictation

Enable voice input to let visitors speak their messages instead of typing. When enabled, visitors see a microphone button in the chat interface that activates their device's native speech recognition.

**How It Works**:

* Visitors tap the microphone button to start speaking
* Speech is transcribed to text in real-time using the device's built-in speech recognition
* Recording automatically stops when the visitor finishes speaking
* The transcribed text appears in the input field, where visitors can edit before sending
* Works on both web browsers and mobile devices that support speech recognition

**Benefits**:

* **Accessibility**: Makes your agent accessible to visitors who prefer voice input or have difficulty typing
* **Mobile Convenience**: Ideal for visitors on mobile devices where typing can be cumbersome
* **Hands-Free Input**: Visitors can engage with your agent while multitasking
* **Natural Expression**: Some visitors express themselves more naturally through speech than text

**Language Support**: Dictation automatically uses the agent's default language setting for speech recognition.


# Evaluations
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/evaluations

Test your agent's performance with automated scenarios and AI-powered scoring

Evaluations let you create automated test scenarios for your agent so you can measure its performance before and after changes. You describe a user scenario, define what success looks like, and Dimedove simulates a full conversation, then scores the result against your criteria.

## How evaluations work

Each evaluation follows a three-step lifecycle:

1. **Define** the scenario and success criteria for a test case.
2. **Run** the evaluation. Dimedove simulates a realistic user conversation with your agent, then an independent AI judge scores the transcript.
3. **Review** the results: an overall score, a pass/partial/fail verdict, and a per-criterion breakdown explaining exactly what worked and what did not.

Evaluations run against your agent's current configuration (including the published version, instructions, knowledge base, and tasks). They do not affect your inbox, contacts, or production conversations.

## Creating an evaluation

1. Navigate to the **Evaluations** section in your agent workspace.
2. Click **Add evaluation**.
3. Dimedove creates a new evaluation and opens its configuration view.
4. Fill in the fields described below, then save.

You can create as many evaluations as your plan allows. A usage counter shows how many you have used out of your plan limit.

## Configuring your scenario

The **Scenario** field describes who the simulated user is and what they are trying to accomplish. Think of it as stage directions for a realistic visitor.

Write your scenario in natural language. Be specific about the user's situation, needs, and behavior so the simulation produces a meaningful test. For example:

* "A marketing manager at a mid-size SaaS company exploring Dimedove for the first time. They want to understand pricing, how the platform compares to their current solution, and whether it can handle their volume of 500 monthly leads."
* "A small business owner who heard about Dimedove from a colleague. They are not very technical and want to know how quickly they can get started, what kind of results to expect, and whether there is a free trial."

The simulated user stays in character throughout the conversation, writing naturally (including occasional typos or informal phrasing) and reacting realistically to your agent's responses.

## Defining success criteria

The **Success criteria** field tells the evaluation judge what a passing conversation looks like. The judge evaluates the full transcript against each criterion you define.

Describe what a successful interaction looks like in your own words. Be concrete and specific so the judge has clear signals to assess. For example:

* "The agent identifies the visitor's company size and use case within the first few exchanges."
* "The agent recommends the correct plan based on the visitor's stated needs."
* "The agent collects the visitor's name and email before the conversation ends."
* "The agent maintains a friendly, consultative tone and avoids being pushy."

Criteria can be high-level ("qualifies the lead properly") or specific ("asks about monthly lead volume before recommending a plan"). The judge evaluates at the appropriate level of specificity for each criterion.

## Max turns

The **Max turns** setting controls how many back-and-forth exchanges the simulated conversation can have, from 1 to 10 (default: 5). The simulated user may also end the conversation naturally before the maximum is reached if the interaction comes to a logical conclusion.

Set a higher turn count for complex scenarios (multi-step troubleshooting, detailed qualification flows) and a lower count for simple ones (quick FAQ lookups, single-question tests).

## Running evaluations

**Run a single evaluation** by clicking the play button next to it in the list view, or the **Run** button at the top of the evaluation detail view.

**Run all evaluations** at once from the list view. Dimedove queues every active evaluation and runs them in the background.

An evaluation requires a scenario, success criteria, and a max turns value greater than zero before it can be run.

## Understanding results

When a run completes, the evaluation judge produces three things:

### Score and verdict

The judge assigns a score from 0 to 100 representing how well your agent performed against your success criteria:

* **Pass** (70-100): Most or all criteria were met. Your agent handled the scenario well.
* **Partial** (40-69): Some criteria were met, but there are noticeable gaps.
* **Fail** (0-39): Few criteria were met. The agent needs significant improvement for this scenario.

A colored status dot provides a quick visual indicator: green for pass, yellow for partial, red for fail.

### Evaluation reasoning

A detailed explanation of the judge's overall assessment. This section cites specific parts of the conversation to support its conclusions. You can expand or collapse the reasoning for easier scanning.

### Criteria breakdown

Each success criterion you defined is listed individually with a pass or fail status and a brief explanation of why it was or was not met. This breakdown makes it straightforward to identify exactly which aspects of your agent's behavior need attention.

## Conversation transcript

Every completed run includes the full conversation transcript between the simulated user and your agent. Open a run's details to read the exchange turn by turn. The transcript helps you understand the context behind each score, especially when a criterion was partially met or missed.

## Run history

The **Runs** tab on an evaluation's detail view shows every past run with its status, date, score, and verdict. Click **View** on any completed run to open its full results, including the evaluation reasoning, criteria breakdown, and conversation transcript.

Use run history to track how your agent's performance evolves over time as you refine its configuration.

## Best practices

* Write scenarios that reflect your actual visitors. Base them on real conversations from your inbox to test the situations your agent encounters most.
* Start with 3 to 5 core scenarios covering your most important use cases (lead qualification, pricing questions, support issues), then expand as you refine your agent.
* After changing your agent's instructions, tone, or knowledge base, re-run your evaluations to verify the changes did not introduce regressions.
* Use specific, measurable success criteria. "The agent is helpful" is hard to evaluate objectively. "The agent provides the correct return policy and offers to initiate a return" gives the judge clear signals to assess.
* Review the conversation transcript when a criterion fails, not just the verdict. The transcript shows exactly where the conversation went off track.
* Pair evaluations with [Versions](/platform/agents/versions) to test a draft configuration before publishing it to production.


# Identity
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/identity

Configure your agent's identity and how it presents itself

Define your agent's core identity to ensure consistent and on-brand interactions with prospects and customers.

### Name

Internal identifier for your agent within the Dimedove platform. This is only visible to you and your team for organization and reporting purposes.

### Business Name

Your company name as the agent will reference it in conversations. This appears when your agent mentions your business to prospects and customers.

### Display Name

The name your agent uses when introducing itself to visitors. Leave blank for a generic assistant approach, or provide a specific name for a more personalized experience.

### Description

Your agent's role, purpose, and behavioral guidelines. This is the most important configuration as it shapes how your agent understands its job, responds to inquiries, and maintains your brand voice throughout all interactions.


# Install
Source: https://docs.dimedove.com/platform/agents/install

Deploy your agent on your website and configure security, country restrictions, and legal terms

The Install page is where you deploy your agent and configure its security and access settings. Add the messenger widget to your website, restrict which domains and countries can access it, and optionally require visitors to accept your legal terms before chatting.

## Setup

Dimedove provides a JavaScript widget that you add to your website. Copy the installation code from the Install page and paste it into your site's HTML:

```html theme={"system"}
<dimedove-messenger agent-id="YOUR_AGENT_ID" publishable-key="YOUR_PUBLISHABLE_KEY" />
<script
  src="https://unpkg.com/@dimedove/messenger@latest/dist/messenger.js"
  crossorigin="anonymous"
  async
></script>
```

The snippet includes your agent's unique ID and publishable key. The messenger script loads asynchronously so it does not block your page from rendering.

For more advanced configuration options, consult the [Developer Guides](/developer/messenger/overview).

## Allowed origins

Allowed origins restrict which domains can host your messenger widget. This prevents unauthorized websites from embedding your agent.

* Enter one or more domains (for example, `example.com` or `app.example.com`).
* Wildcard subdomains are supported (for example, `*.example.com` matches any subdomain).
* Subpages and directories on allowed domains are automatically permitted.
* Leave the field empty to allow all domains.

It is recommended to configure allowed origins for any production deployment.

## Country restrictions

Country restrictions let you control where your messenger is accessible based on the visitor's geographic location. This is useful for compliance, regional availability, or targeting specific markets.

There are three modes:

* **None** (default): No geographic restrictions. The messenger is accessible worldwide.
* **Allow**: Only visitors from the selected countries can access the messenger. All other countries are blocked.
* **Block**: Visitors from the selected countries are blocked. All other countries can access the messenger.

When you select Allow or Block, a country selector appears where you can search and pick one or more countries.

If you set the mode to Allow or Block but do not select any countries, the restriction automatically resets to None when you save.

## Confidentiality

Require visitors to accept your privacy policy and terms of service before starting a conversation. When enabled, the messenger displays a consent prompt linking to your legal documents.

To configure:

1. Toggle **Require accept terms** on.
2. Enter your **Privacy Policy URL**, your **Terms of Service URL**, or both. At least one is required.
3. Dimedove automatically generates a consent message that links to the URLs you provided. A preview of the message is displayed below the fields.

The generated consent message uses your business name (if configured) and links directly to your legal documents.
